source_text: Attende sane nunc quale sit, quod de tua opinione colligitur; videlicet operiendum pudore non esse, quidquid bonum creditur. Nos autem docuimus voluntatem illam naturaliter sexibus inditam, tam malam non esse, quam ad Dei operam pertinentem. Ac per hoc tu aut impietatem tuam deseres, aut pudorem. Sed quid nos haec autem? Si mutabit Aethiops pellem suam, aut pardus varietatem [n69] ; ita et tu a Manichaeorum mysteriis elueris.
pass_a_gloss: Attend now, to be sure, of what sort that is which is gathered from your opinion; namely that whatever is believed good is not to be covered by modesty. But we have taught that that will naturally put into the sexes is as not evil as it belongs to God's work. And through this you will either desert your impiety, or your modesty. But what is this to us? If the Ethiopian will change his skin, or the leopard its spots; so also will you be washed from the mysteries of the Manichaeans.

lemmas.lexica: Blaise Manichaeus; Julian's polemic label vs natural evil
LS naturalis; Blaise malum naturale=evil as a nature
LS voluntas=will, wish; Blaise moral will
LS/Blaise natura=created constitution, not 'original sin' itself
LS malum; Blaise malum naturale vs malum voluntatis

pass_b_english: Now consider what follows from your opinion: whatever is believed good should not be covered out of modesty. But I have shown that this desire naturally implanted in the sexes is not evil, since it belongs to God’s work. Accordingly, you must abandon either your impiety or your modesty. But why do I say this? “If the Ethiopian changes his skin or the leopard its spots” (Jeremiah 13:23), then you too will be washed clean of the Manichaean mysteries.

choices.why: Julian's definition of sin is an act of will. Keep 'will' rather than later 'free will' system language unless liberum arbitrium is present.
Julian's Manichaean charge: an evil that is a nature, not a will's act.
Julian's charge against Augustine: treating evil as a nature rather than as will.

anf_compare.notes: Victorian English of some of Julian survives inside NPNF Augustine (chiefly On Marriage and Concupiscence and related anti-Pelagian books). NPNF was not copied. Pass A is a literal gloss of Augustinus.it Latin of Julian's words only; Augustine's replies in the same locus are excluded.
